notes: Summary: Ceres builds search/QA for in-house counsel. Heavy emphasis on accuracy for precedents; downstream workflows require deterministic reranking for auditability.
Search volume profile: peak 12k queries/day, baseline 3-5k. 3M indexed chunks anticipated (sentence-level + clause-level).
Latency targets: 95th percentile < 200ms for top-K retrieval path; end-to-end (retrieve + rerank) <= 600ms where possible.
Cost sensitivity: Legal ops wants predictable per-query unit economics; internal target <$0.05/query at baseline load; willing to pay more for private deployment SLA.

Preferred vector DBs: evaluating pgvector for residency/on-prem, Weaviate for semantic-ML features, and Elastic for metadata-rich filters. Pinecone considered for hosted convenience but legal wary of SaaS residency.

Connector requirements (customer): upsert throughput >= 50k vectors/hour for initial ingest, bulk upsert with idempotency, delta updates for refresh, schema-level metadata filtering (date, jurisdiction, client-id), boolean and range filters exposed to Redwood query planner.

Reranking flow: initial ANN recall (HNSW/IVF) -> shortlist 100 -> cross-encoder rerank (on Redwood runtime) -> deterministic scoring stored with audit id. Need support for storing rerank scores and trace IDs back into vector DB or audit log.
Quality controls requested: evaluation harness, guardrail to detect rerank regressions, daily QA run on gold prompt set; Redwood Optimize suggested for automated suggestions.

Integration notes: must support pgvector COPY/SQL bulk loads, Weaviate’s import API, and Elastic k-NN mapping. Need sample connector playbooks and a migration strategy for moving vectors between DBs without re-embedding where possible.
Quote from Head of Engineering: 'We need deterministic reranks for compliance. Black-box SaaS that can’t export vectors is a red flag.'
Drive: pricing-deck-v2 and security-FAQ shared (drive/redwood/ceres/pricing-deck-v2, drive/redwood/ceres/security-faq.pdf).

vector_requirements: Scale: target 3M vectors initially, plan to expand to 10M in 12 months; retention of raw documents + vector shards required
Indexing SLA: bulk ingest window 8 hours for 3M with monitored progress; ability to throttle live upserts without impacting query latency
ANN details: must support metric selection (cosine, dot, l2) per-collection; ability to expose HNSW params for tuning recall/latency tradeoffs
Filtering: multi-attribute filters (jurisdiction, practice_area, client, doc_date) applied at ANN retrieval stage to reduce reranker load
Consistency: upsert idempotency, vector versioning, tombstones for deletions, and soft-delete for audit
Hybrid reranking: connector must allow retrieving candidate vectors + metadata + raw text payload for cross-encoder scoring without extra roundtrips
Monitoring: per-query latency, 99/95/50 percentiles, QPS, CPU/GPU utilization for dedicated nodes, and cost-per-query breakdown
Export/migration: ability to export vectors in standardized format (numpy/csv) with metadata mapping; snapshots for backup and legal eDiscovery
Security/ops: TLS for in-transit, at-rest encryption, fine-grained RBAC on namespaces/collections, and KMS integration for keys
Connector ops expectations: sample terraform module, Helm chart or docker-compose for pgvector/Weaviate; documented upgrade path and breaking-change policy
poc_success_criteria: Recall/precision: top-20 shortlist must achieve >= 0.78 MRR on our gold set
Latency: 95p retrieval < 200ms on dedicated infra; end-to-end rerank < 600ms for 95p
Cost: projected cost <= $0.05/query at 5k Q/day baseline (including retrieve, rerank compute, and storage amortized)
Security: pass internal security checklist items SSO/KMS/audit logging and legal sign-off on data residency
Operational: connector handles 50k upserts/hour with <2% failure rate; snapshot export completes within agreed SLA
